name: zzAN1_avatar

tests.name: the editor exports the raw frame instrument
there are Project Avatar figures to spawn
the world settled before rung zero was taken

detail.note: rung zero is what every other rung is compared against, and it has always been the earliest and least settled reading in this job. A fixed wait is a guess about when the world has arrived; this waits for three reads to agree and voids if they never do.

tests.name: r.Shadow.Virtual.Enable took the value it was given
r.DistanceFields took the value it was given

detail.note: the rung is VOID rather than reported: an unrecognised cvar leaves the world exactly as it was, and publishing that as a toggled measurement is how a knob that does nothing gets credited with a result.

tests.name: the run is settled enough to compare rungs at all

detail.note: rung zero is the value every other rung is compared against, so a spike in it poisons the whole ladder. A worst frame more than ten times the median means the world was still arriving; a rung with under thirty frames means the stat overlay was off for most of its window. Either way the numbers below describe this machine's evening, not avatars.

tests.name: the run reproduced the finding it was built to explain

detail.note: if one avatar is NOT expensive on this run, nothing below means anything and the 16:33 reading was a property of that session rather than of avatars.

tests.name: the cost at one avatar is a switch rather than a gradient

detail.reading: NOT A SWITCH: the cost declines gradually across the rungs, so no path is turning on above one instance and the explanation is elsewhere.
